intro.title: Observability — Logs, Metrics & Traces
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple observability dashboard to monitor a simulated web service. You will learn the core concepts of observability: logs for recording events, metrics for measuring performance, and traces for tracking requests. The main technologies involved are structured logging, basic metric collection, and distributed tracing. By the end, you will understand how these three pillars work together to provide visibility into system health and behavior. This foundational knowledge is essential for debugging and maintaining reliable production systems.
intro.usecase: In production systems, observability tools are critical for monitoring application health and troubleshooting issues. Developers use log aggregation dashboards like Splunk or Datadog to search through application logs when debugging errors. Metrics dashboards with charts and graphs in tools like Grafana or Prometheus visualize system performance trends over time. Distributed tracing interfaces in tools like Jaeger or Zipkin help engineers follow request flows across microservices to identify bottlenecks. These observability interfaces are essential for maintaining reliable, high-performance applications in production environments.
